001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.io.FileDescriptor;
004import java.io.Flushable;
005import java.io.IOException;
006import java.io.OutputStream;
007import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
008import java.net.URI;
009import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
010import java.nio.charset.Charset;
011import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
012import java.util.Objects;
013import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;
014
015import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
016
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogAppender.AppenderFlag;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.Buffer;
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.BufferHints;
020import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
021
022/**
023 * A resource that can be written to usually in binary. In other logging frameworks this
024 * is often called an "Appender" not be confused with RainbowGum's appenders. LogOutputs
025 * will be written synchronously by the appender either through locks or some other
026 * mechanism so other than output external specific locking (e.g file locking or db
027 * transaction) the output does not have to deal with that. <strong> In other words there
028 * will be no overlapping write/flush/close calls as the appender and publisher combo
029 * promises that. </strong>
030 * <p>
031 * To simplyfy flushing and corruption prevention each call to the write methods MUST be
032 * the contents of the entire event! However the output should not flush unless
033 * {@link #flush()} is called by the appender. That is the appender
034 * <strong>usually</strong> decides when to flush.
035 * <p>
036 * The write methods do not throw {@link IOException} on purpose as it is implementations
037 * responsibility to handle errors and to be resilient on their own.
038 * <p>
039 * An output that needs a particular kind of encoding - or cannot function with just any
040 * encoder - implements {@link ProvidesEncoder} to supply its own, either as a mandatory,
041 * non-overridable choice or as an overridable default; see {@link ProvidesEncoder} for
042 * details.
043 *
044 * @see LogOutput.OutputProvider
045 * @see LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder
046 * @see Buffer
047 * @see AppenderFlag#DISABLE_IMMEDIATE_FLUSH
048 * @apiNote if for some reason the output needs to share events with other threads call
049 * {@link LogEvent#freeze()} which will return an immutable event.
050 */
051public interface LogOutput extends LogLifecycle, Flushable {
052
053        /**
054         * {@link FileDescriptor#err} URI scheme.
055         */
056        static final String STDERR_SCHEME = "stderr";
057
058        /**
059         * {@link FileDescriptor#out} URI scheme.
060         */
061        static final String STDOUT_SCHEME = "stdout";
062
063        /**
064         * File URI scheme.
065         */
066        static final String FILE_SCHEME = "file";
067
068        /**
069         * Standard OUT URI.
070         */
071        static final URI STDOUT_URI = URI.create(STDOUT_SCHEME + ":///");
072
073        /**
074         * Standard ERR URI
075         */
076        static final URI STDERR_URI = URI.create(STDERR_SCHEME + ":///");
077
078        /**
079         * Provides a lazy loaded output from a URI.
080         * @param uri uri.
081         * @return provider of output.
082         * @apiNote the provider may throw an {@link UncheckedIOException}.
083         */
084        private static LogProvider<LogOutput> of(URI uri) {
085                /*
086                 * TODO this should probably be public.
087                 */
088                return of(LogProviderRef.of(uri));
089        }
090
091        /**
092         * Provides a lazy loaded output from a URI.
093         * @param ref uri.
094         * @return provider of output.
095         * @apiNote the provider may throw an {@link UncheckedIOException}.
096         */
097        public static LogProvider<LogOutput> of(LogProviderRef ref) {
098                return (s, c) -> {
099                        return c.outputRegistry().provide(ref).provide(s, c);
100                };
101        }
102
103        /**
104         * Standard out output. The default implementation <em>uses whatever is set to
105         * {@link System#out} at provision time</em>. <strong>If {@link System#out} is rebound
106         * the output will not be updated!</strong>
107         * @return output.
108         */
109        public static LogProvider<LogOutput> ofStandardOut() {
110                return of(LogOutput.STDOUT_URI);
111        }
112
113        /**
114         * Standard err output. The default implementation <em>uses whatever is set to
115         * {@link System#err} at provision time</em>. <strong>If {@link System#err} is rebound
116         * the output will not be updated!</strong>
117         * @return output.
118         */
119        public static LogProvider<LogOutput> ofStandardErr() {
120                return of(LogOutput.STDERR_URI);
121        }
122
123        /**
124         * Finds output based on URI.
125         */
126        public interface OutputProvider {
127
128                /**
129                 * Creates an output ready to be injected with config.
130                 * @param ref a URI reference to the output.
131                 * @return provider of output.
132                 */
133                LogProvider<LogOutput> provide(LogProviderRef ref);
134
135        }
136
137        /**
138         * Marks an output that supplies its own {@link LogEncoder} instead of relying
139         * entirely on {@link LogAppender#APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY} or
140         * {@link LogEncoderRegistry#encoderForOutputType(OutputType)}. {@link #policy()}
141         * decides whether that encoder can still be overridden:
142         * <ul>
143         * <li>{@link Policy#MANDATORY}: {@link #encoder(String, LogConfig)} is the only
144         * encoder this output will ever use. Configuring another one anyway -
145         * programmatically via {@link LogAppender.Builder#encoder}, or via
146         * {@link LogAppender#APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY} - is a
147         * {@link LogProperty.ValidationException}, not a silent override.
148         * <li>{@link Policy#DEFAULT}: {@link #encoder(String, LogConfig)} is used only if
149         * nothing else is configured; either of the above always wins over it.
150         * </ul>
151         * Neither policy is consulted at all if an output does not implement this interface
152         * in the first place - such an output has no opinion on its own encoder, and
153         * resolution proceeds exactly as if this interface did not exist.
154         *
155         * @see LogAppender.Builder#build()
156         */
157        public interface ProvidesEncoder {
158
159                /**
160                 * The encoder this output supplies, given the same {@code name}/{@code config}
161                 * the output itself was provided with.
162                 * @param name appender name.
163                 * @param config config.
164                 * @return encoder, see {@link #policy()} for whether it can be overridden.
165                 * @apiNote this method is only ever called once per appender resolution, so an
166                 * implementation does not need to memoize the returned encoder itself.
167                 */
168                LogEncoder encoder(String name, LogConfig config);
169
170                /**
171                 * Whether {@link #encoder(String, LogConfig)} can be overridden by an explicitly
172                 * configured encoder. Defaults to {@link Policy#DEFAULT} - an implementation only
173                 * needs to override this to return {@link Policy#MANDATORY}.
174                 * @return policy.
175                 */
176                default Policy policy() {
177                        return Policy.DEFAULT;
178                }
179
180                /**
181                 * Whether a {@link ProvidesEncoder}'s
182                 * {@link ProvidesEncoder#encoder(String, LogConfig)} can be overridden by
183                 * another, explicitly configured encoder.
184                 */
185                enum Policy {
186
187                        /**
188                         * The output's own encoder is the only one allowed. Explicitly configuring
189                         * another encoder anyway, programmatically or via property, is a validation
190                         * failure rather than a silent override.
191                         */
192                        MANDATORY,
193
194                        /**
195                         * The output's own encoder is used only as a fallback: any explicitly
196                         * configured encoder, programmatic or property, wins over it.
197                         */
198                        DEFAULT;
199
200                }
201
202        }
203
204        /**
205         * The content type of the binary data passed to the output from an encoder.
206         */
207        public interface ContentType {
208
209                /**
210                 * Content type of binary datay passed to output.
211                 * @return content type.
212                 */
213                String contentType();
214
215                /**
216                 * The charset the bytes are encoded with, or <code>null</code> if there is no
217                 * single fixed charset for this content type. Both built-in
218                 * {@link StandardContentType} constants are always {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}
219                 * - {@link StandardContentType#APPLICATION_JSON} by spec, and
220                 * {@link StandardContentType#TEXT_PLAIN} because UTF-8 is standard enough on
221                 * modern Java (e.g. {@code String#getBytes()}'s no-charset overload) to treat as
222                 * the assumed default rather than "unspecified" - an encoder actually configured
223                 * with a different charset (see {@link LogEncoder#builder(LogFormatter)}) reports
224                 * a different content type instead, not {@link StandardContentType#TEXT_PLAIN}.
225                 * @return charset or <code>null</code> if not fixed/known.
226                 */
227                @Nullable Charset charsetOrNull();
228
229                /**
230                 * Finds the matching {@link StandardContentType} for the given content type and
231                 * charset if one exists, otherwise creates a new plain {@link ContentType}.
232                 * @param contentType content type, e.g. <code>text/plain</code>.
233                 * @param charsetOrNull charset or <code>null</code> if not fixed/known.
234                 * @return a {@link StandardContentType} if one matches, otherwise a plain
235                 * {@link ContentType}.
236                 */
237                static ContentType of(String contentType, @Nullable Charset charsetOrNull) {
238                        for (var standard : StandardContentType.values()) {
239                                if (standard.contentType().equals(contentType)
240                                                && Objects.equals(standard.charsetOrNull(), charsetOrNull)) {
241                                        return standard;
242                                }
243                        }
244                        return new SimpleContentType(contentType, charsetOrNull);
245                }
246
247                /**
248                 * Builtin content types.
249                 *
250                 * @apiNote additional "standard" content types maybe added in the future before
251                 * 1.0 thus one should expect the number of enum symbols to change and is not safe
252                 * to pattern match on without a default.
253                 */
254                @CaseChanging
255                public enum StandardContentType implements ContentType {
256
257                        /**
258                         * text/plain
259                         */
260                        TEXT_PLAIN() {
261                                @Override
262                                public String contentType() {
263                                        return "text/plain";
264                                }
265
266                                @Override
267                                public Charset charsetOrNull() {
268                                        return StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
269                                }
270                        },
271                        /**
272                         * application/json
273                         */
274                        APPLICATION_JSON() {
275                                @Override
276                                public String contentType() {
277                                        return "application/json";
278                                }
279
280                                @Override
281                                public Charset charsetOrNull() {
282                                        return StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
283                                }
284                        }
285
286                }
287
288        }
289
290        /**
291         * The uri of the output.
292         * @return uri.
293         * @throws UnsupportedOperationException if this output does not support URI
294         * representation.
295         *
296         */
297        public URI uri() throws UnsupportedOperationException;
298
299        @Override
300        default void start(LogConfig config) {
301        }
302
303        /**
304         * Write a batch of events by default calls
305         * {@link #write(LogEvent[], int, LogEncoder, Buffer)}. <strong>DO NOT MODIFY THE
306         * ARRAY</strong>. Do not use the <code>length</code> of the passed in array but
307         * instead use <code>count</code> parameter.
308         * @param events an array guaranteed to be smaller than count.
309         * @param count the number of items.
310         * @param encoder encoder to use for encoding.
311         */
312        default void write(LogEvent[] events, int count, LogEncoder encoder) {
313                try (var buffer = encoder.buffer(this.bufferHints())) {
314                        write(events, count, encoder, buffer);
315                }
316        }
317
318        /**
319         * Write a batch of events reusing the provided buffer and by default calling
320         * {@link #write(LogEvent, Buffer)} for each event synchronously.
321         * <p>
322         * The batching is usually a result of an asynchronous publisher so the maximum size
323         * is configured there with bufferSize. If this method is implemented there are some
324         * caveats.
325         * <p>
326         * <strong>DO NOT MODIFY THE ARRAY</strong>. It is reused. Do not use the
327         * <code>length</code> of the passed in array but instead use <code>count</code>
328         * parameter. Consequently do not share the array or buffer with other threads however
329         * individual events can be shared by calling {@link LogEvent#freeze()} to guarantee
330         * that which is a safe no-op if it is already immutable.
331         * <p>
332         * If the output plans on grouping the events into a single blob (byte array or byte
333         * buffer) a different output can be passed to the encoder other than itself (which is
334         * the default).
335         * @param events an array guaranteed to be smaller than count.
336         * @param count the number of items.
337         * @param encoder encoder to use for encoding.
338         * @param buffer buffer to reuse. Do not share it with other threads!
339         * @apiNote If the output wants to fan-out or encode with other threads the buffer
340         * passed should not be used and instead {@link LogEncoder#buffer(BufferHints)} should
341         * be called to get a new buffer for each thread. This is generally not desirable for
342         * most resources such as a file or database as sending a batch is much faster (single
343         * writer principle).
344         */
345        default void write(LogEvent[] events, int count, LogEncoder encoder, Buffer buffer) {
346                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
347                        buffer.clear();
348                        var event = events[i];
349                        encoder.encode(event, buffer);
350                        write(event, buffer);
351                }
352        }
353
354        /**
355         * Writes a prepared buffer and by default drains the buffer to this output.
356         * @param event event.
357         * @param buffer buffer that is already filled. Do not share it with other threads!
358         * @apiNote the buffer already has the encoding.
359         */
360        default void write(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
361                buffer.drain(this, event);
362        }
363
364        /**
365         * Writes a string and by default with charset {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}.
366         * @param event event associated with string.
367         * @param s string.
368         */
369        default void write(LogEvent event, String s) {
370                write(event, s.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), ContentType.StandardContentType.TEXT_PLAIN);
371        }
372
373        /**
374         * Analogous to {@link OutputStream#write(byte[])}.
375         * @param event event associated with bytes.
376         * @param bytes data to be written.
377         * @param contentType content type of the bytes.
378         */
379        default void write(LogEvent event, byte[] bytes, ContentType contentType) {
380                write(event, bytes, 0, bytes.length, contentType);
381        }
382
383        /**
384         * Analogous to {@link OutputStream#write(byte[], int, int)}.
385         * @param event event associated with bytes.
386         * @param bytes data to be written.
387         * @param off offset.
388         * @param len length.
389         * @param contentType content type of the bytes.
390         */
391        public void write(LogEvent event, byte[] bytes, int off, int len, ContentType contentType);
392
393        /**
394         * Write event with byte buffer. The buffer is expected to be ready for reading in the
395         * standard {@link ByteBuffer} idiom: <code>position</code> at the start of the
396         * content and <code>limit</code> at its end (e.g. just {@linkplain ByteBuffer#flip()
397         * flipped} after being filled, or created with {@link ByteBuffer#wrap(byte[])}).
398         * @param event event.
399         * @param buf byte buffer ready for reading (flipped).
400         * @param contentType content type of the buf
401         */
402        default void write(LogEvent event, ByteBuffer buf, ContentType contentType) {
403                byte[] arr = new byte[buf.remaining()];
404                buf.get(arr);
405                write(event, arr, contentType);
406        }
407
408        /**
409         * Flushes if the output is maintaining a buffer. By default an appender will call
410         * this after each event in synchronous mode or after a batched group of events if in
411         * asynchronous mode unless {@link LogAppender.AppenderFlag#DISABLE_IMMEDIATE_FLUSH}
412         * is set.
413         * @see LogAppender.AppenderFlag#DISABLE_IMMEDIATE_FLUSH
414         */
415        @Override
416        public void flush();
417
418        /**
419         * Gross categorization of an output.
420         * @return output type.
421         */
422        public OutputType type();
423
424        /**
425         * Hints to the buffer like what write style of the output and maximum buffer size.
426         * The output should still honor all write methods but this signals to the encoder
427         * which style it prefers.
428         * @return write mode.
429         */
430        default BufferHints bufferHints() {
431                return WriteMethod.BYTES;
432        }
433
434        /**
435         * Attempts to reopen the output if supported and <strong>SHOULD only be called by the
436         * appender</strong>! This call is mainly used for external log rotation systems such
437         * as logrotate or an aggregator agent. The default implementation does nothing -
438         * reopening is opt-in per output.
439         * @throws RuntimeException implementations are free to throw on failure - the caller
440         * (the appender) is responsible for catching this and reporting it to the alert
441         * system rather than propagating it.
442         */
443        default void reopen() {
444        }
445
446        /**
447         * The preferred write style of an output. The output should still honor all write
448         * methods but this signals to the encoder which style it prefers.
449         */
450        public enum WriteMethod implements BufferHints {
451
452                /**
453                 * Prefer calling {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, String)}.
454                 */
455                STRING,
456                /**
457                 * Prefer calling {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, byte[], ContentType)} or
458                 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, byte[], int, int, ContentType)}.
459                 */
460                BYTES,
461                /**
462                 * Prefer calling {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, ContentType)}.
463                 */
464                BYTE_BUFFER;
465
466                @Override
467                public WriteMethod writeMethod() {
468                        return this;
469                }
470
471        }
472
473        /**
474         * Output type useful for defaults and categorization.
475         */
476        @CaseChanging
477        public enum OutputType {
478
479                /**
480                 * Standard out.
481                 */
482                CONSOLE_OUT,
483                /**
484                 * Standard err.
485                 */
486                CONSOLE_ERR,
487                /**
488                 * Output targets a file.
489                 */
490                FILE,
491                /**
492                 * Output targets something over a network.
493                 */
494                NETWORK,
495                /**
496                 * Output targets in memory.
497                 */
498                MEMORY;
499
500        }
501
502        /**
503         * Will close the output and should only be called by the owning appender.
504         */
505        @Override
506        void close();
507
508        /**
509         * Marker interface that the output is thread safe.
510         */
511        public interface ThreadSafeLogOutput extends LogOutput {
512
513        }
514
515        /**
516         * Abstract output on output stream.
517         */
518        abstract class AbstractOutputStreamOutput implements LogOutput {
519
520                /**
521                 * passed in uri
522                 */
523                protected final URI uri;
524
525                /**
526                 * output stream to write to.
527                 */
528                protected final OutputStream outputStream;
529
530                /*
531                 * A log call can still be in flight (e.g. routed through SLF4J from a shutdown
532                 * hook) after something outside the normal appender/publisher lifecycle - like
533                 * LoggingSystem.cleanUp() - has already closed this output directly. Once closed,
534                 * write/flush become no-ops instead of throwing so that race does not surface as
535                 * an uncaught exception on whatever thread is still trying to log.
536                 */
537                private final AtomicBoolean closed = new AtomicBoolean();
538
539                /**
540                 * Adapts an OutputStream to an Output.
541                 * @param uri usually comes from output registry.
542                 * @param outputStream output stream to adapt.
543                 */
544                protected AbstractOutputStreamOutput(URI uri, OutputStream outputStream) {
545                        super();
546                        this.uri = uri;
547                        this.outputStream = outputStream;
548                }
549
550                @Override
551                public URI uri() {
552                        return uri;
553                }
554
555                @Override
556                public void write(LogEvent event, byte[] bytes, int off, int len, ContentType contentType) {
557                        if (closed.get()) {
558                                return;
559                        }
560                        try {
561                                outputStream.write(bytes, off, len);
562                        }
563                        catch (IOException e) {
564                                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
565                        }
566                }
567
568                @Override
569                public void flush() {
570                        if (closed.get()) {
571                                return;
572                        }
573                        try {
574                                outputStream.flush();
575                        }
576                        catch (IOException e) {
577                                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
578                        }
579                }
580
581                @Override
582                public void close() {
583                        if (!closed.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
584                                return;
585                        }
586                        try {
587                                outputStream.close();
588                        }
589                        catch (IOException e) {
590                                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
591                        }
592                }
593
594                @Override
595                public BufferHints bufferHints() {
596                        return WriteMethod.BYTES;
597                }
598
599        }
600
601}
602
603/**
604 * A plain {@link LogOutput.ContentType} for content types not covered by
605 * {@link LogOutput.ContentType.StandardContentType}. Created via
606 * {@link LogOutput.ContentType#of(String, Charset)} (or reuses a matching
607 * {@link LogOutput.ContentType.StandardContentType} instead if one matches).
608 *
609 * @param contentType content type, e.g. <code>text/plain</code>.
610 * @param charsetOrNull charset or <code>null</code> if not fixed/known.
611 */
612record SimpleContentType(String contentType, @Nullable Charset charsetOrNull) implements LogOutput.ContentType {
613}
614
615class StdOutOutput extends LogOutput.AbstractOutputStreamOutput {
616
617        public StdOutOutput() {
618                super(LogOutput.STDOUT_URI, Objects.requireNonNull(System.out));
619        }
620
621        @Override
622        public LogOutput.OutputType type() {
623                return OutputType.CONSOLE_OUT;
624        }
625
626        @Override
627        public void close() {
628        }
629
630}
631
632class StdErrOutput extends LogOutput.AbstractOutputStreamOutput {
633
634        protected StdErrOutput() {
635                super(LogOutput.STDERR_URI, Objects.requireNonNull(System.err));
636        }
637
638        @Override
639        public OutputType type() {
640                return OutputType.CONSOLE_ERR;
641        }
642
643        @Override
644        public void close() {
645        }
646
